review.summary: This PR adds an admin analytics dashboard (client charts + server aggregation endpoints) and public view tracking. Route wiring is sound (analytics router mounted behind `auth`, validators on every endpoint), but the new view-recording endpoint logs bearer tokens, several date-parsing paths accept invalid input, dedup is keyed on client-controlled data with a race, and the view metrics scope blogs by creation date in a way that drops most real views.

findings.title: Bearer tokens written to logs on every view request
findings.rationale: `console.log('[analytics] auth header:', req.headers.authorization)` runs inside `recordView`, which is wired to the public route `POST /:blogId/view` (blogRoutes.js line 24). Any request carrying an `Authorization` header — e.g., a logged-in admin browsing the public blog while the client attaches the token globally — writes a valid admin JWT to server logs in plaintext. Anyone with log access (log aggregation, crash reporters, ops) obtains a working admin credential. Delete the line.

findings.title: parseChartDateToRange accepts impossible dates
findings.rationale: For `date=2025-02-30`, `new Date('2025-02-30T00:00:00.000Z')` (line 96) is Invalid Date, but the function still returns `{ from: Invalid Date, to: Invalid Date }` — a truthy object — so `validateDrillDownQuery`'s `if (!range)` guard passes and the request proceeds with a garbage date range instead of the intended 400 (the driver then either errors into a 500 or silently queries a bogus range). The month branch (line 122) has no 1–12 check: `date=2025-13` silently resolves to January 2026, and the week branch (line 111) accepts `2025-W00`/`2025-W99`. Add `isNaN(from.getTime())` checks and range-validate month/week.

findings.title: Custom date ranges exclude the end day
findings.rationale: `parseDate` (line 13) returns UTC midnight, so `?from=2025-01-01&to=2025-01-31` produces `to = 2025-01-31T00:00:00Z` (line 45). Every `viewedAt`/`createdAt: { $lte: to }` filter built from it (buildBlogFilter, buildViewFilter, getTopCommented) then drops all of Jan 31. The drill-down parser treats a day as inclusive (analyticsAggregations.js line 97), so the same date shows different numbers depending on entry point; UTC-midnight parsing also misaligns ranges for non-UTC admins. Use end-of-day (23:59:59.999) for `to`.

findings.title: View dedup keyed on client-supplied values
findings.rationale: `recordView` reads `visitorKey` and `referrerSource` from the request body. Since the dedup key is attacker-chosen, scripting `POST /:blogId/view` with a fresh UUID per request records unlimited views (only the global 300/min limiter caps it), and `referrerSource` is freely spoofable — the advertised duplicate-view prevention and referrer classification are trivially gamed. `viewTracking.js` already implements server-side `computeVisitorKey` (IP+UA hash) and `classifyReferrer` (Referer header); this endpoint ignores both.

findings.title: Check-then-insert race duplicates views
findings.rationale: Two concurrent POSTs with the same visitorKey both pass the `findOne` at line 687 and both execute `BlogView.create` at line 718. The `{ blog, visitorKey, viewedAt }` index (BlogView.js line 30) is not unique, so nothing catches the duplicate — even honest clients double-firing the POST (StrictMode, retries) double-count. Make dedup atomic with a unique partial index or an upsert.

findings.title: recordView diverges from viewTracking.js on dedup scope and admin role
findings.rationale: The controller's dedup query (lines 687-691) omits `isAdminView: false`, so an admin view blocks later same-key views for 24h and admin views are deduped — which `viewTracking.js` (lines 87-93) explicitly skips. Its role check (line 710) accepts only `role === 'admin'` while `viewTracking.isAdminRequest` (line 66) also accepts `'Admin'`. Whichever role string the auth middleware actually issues, one of the two paths misclassifies admin views. Keep one implementation and delete the other.

findings.title: View metrics only count blogs created inside the period
findings.rationale: `buildBlogFilter` scopes blogs by `createdAt: { $gte: from, $lte: to }`, and `getTopViewed` (controller line 358) and `getDrillDown` (lines 599-601) use it for view metrics. With the default 30-day period, a post published two months ago contributes nothing to "top viewed" even if it got every view that week, and a day's drill-down omits older posts' views for that day. If period-scoping is intended for publications metrics, view metrics should scope by view time across all blogs (category filter only).

findings.title: exportCsv runs 2 queries per blog in a serial loop
findings.rationale: For N blogs the export executes 2N sequential `countDocuments` calls (500 blogs → 1000 round-trips); the request will take minutes and likely time out while hammering Mongo. Replace with two `$group by blog` aggregations (views in range, total comments) joined to the blog list.

findings.title: Unescaped $regex from req.query.search
findings.rationale: `blogFilter.title = { $regex: req.query.search, $options: 'i' }` passes raw user input to MongoDB regex. `search=(a+)+$` triggers catastrophic backtracking on the database server (ReDoS), and unescaped metacharacters break literal searches (e.g., `C++`). Admin-gated, so not critical, but escape the input or use `$text` search.

findings.title: CSV formula injection in escapeCSV
findings.rationale: `escapeCSV` neutralizes commas/quotes/newlines but not formula prefixes. A blog title of `=HYPERLINK("http://evil.example","click")` is written verbatim into the export and executes when the CSV opens in Excel/Sheets. Prefix cells starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@` with a `'` (or tab) escape.

findings.title: Array query param crashes validation with a 500
findings.rationale: `GET /analytics/kpis?category=All&category=All` makes Express hand back `['All','All']`; `(...).trim()` throws `TypeError: .trim is not a function`, which surfaces as a 500. (`period` survives repeated params only because `PERIODS.includes` merely returns false.) Type-check/coerce `category` before calling `.trim()`.

findings.title: Global rate limit tripled to serve one feature
findings.rationale: Raising the shared `apiLimiter` from 100 to 300 req/min loosens the backstop for every endpoint (login attempts, comment spam, etc.). A dedicated limiter on the analytics router would keep the global limit intact.

findings.title: Referrer classification by substring match
findings.rationale: `host.includes('x.com')` classifies `netflix.com` as `social`, and `includes('google')` matches `notgoogle.com`. Compare exact hostnames or registrable-domain suffixes instead of substrings.
